title: retained-verification-artefacts-create-durable-correlation-surface

proposition.statement: A relying system must not treat verification evidence retention as privacy-neutral when presentations, status observations, transcripts, identifiers, or related artefacts are retained or aggregated beyond the minimum justified purpose and thereby enable later cross-context reconstruction or sensitive inference.

preconditions: Verification, assurance, audit, or operational processing produces artefacts that can be persisted.
The retained artefacts contain or can be joined through identifiers, timing, proof data, status observations, or contextual metadata.
The applicable purpose does not positively establish the necessity of indefinite or broadly aggregated retention.

trigger.statement: Verification artefacts are persisted or aggregated beyond the justified purpose or retention boundary and become a durable dataset from which otherwise separate interactions can be reconstructed or correlated.

evidence_required.statement: Evidence defining the operational, assurance, audit, legal, or governance purpose and retention bound applicable to each retained artefact.
Evidence identifying which verifier, processor, repository, or evidence service retains and aggregates the artefacts.
Evidence testing whether retained artefacts can be joined across interactions or contexts to create a material correlation or inference surface.
Evidence of retention duration, expiry, deletion, and any later reuse of the retained artefacts.

falsification.condition: The system reports PASS for privacy while retaining verification artefacts beyond the established purpose or retention boundary and those artefacts permit cross-context reconstruction.
Audit or assurance value is asserted as a blanket justification for retaining raw or linkable artefacts when less correlating evidence would satisfy the same stated purpose.

references.note: Repository judgment record for the privacy/correlation tranche.

Research provenance: W3C VC Data Model Threat Model v2.1 privacy threats concerning aggregation, post-presentation use, and observable credential activity; draft/work in progress, not corpus authority.
